title: Allergen immunotherapy (allergy shots or drops)
what: You are given small doses of the allergen, slowly increasing. Your body gets used to it, and the allergy becomes weaker.
why: For allergy to pollen, house dust mites, or insect stings, when the exact allergen is known.
duration: a shot or a tablet under the tongue takes a few minutes, plus about 30 minutes of observation; the course usually lasts 3 to 5 years
tell_doctor: A current asthma or allergy flare-up
A fever, a cold, or an infection
All your medicines, especially for the heart and blood pressure

prepare.title: Season
prepare.text: The course is often started outside the pollen season. The allergist will make the schedule.

prepare.title: Shot day
prepare.text: On the day of the shot, no sauna, hard workouts, or alcohol.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Do not stop your allergy and asthma medicines on your own.

steps: The doctor or nurse asks how you feel
Sometimes your breathing is measured, if you have asthma
You get a shot under the skin of your arm, or a drop or tablet under the tongue
You stay under observation for about 30 minutes
The nurse checks the injection site
You are told the date of your next dose
feel: Redness and itching at the injection site are common
With drops or tablets, an itchy mouth in the first days
after: Do not leave the clinic before the observation time is over
That day, no hard exercise, sauna, or alcohol
Write your reactions in the diary
Do not skip doses, since the effect depends on regularity
red_flags: Trouble breathing, swelling of the lips or tongue, or a rash all over: call emergency services
Heavy swelling at the injection site, larger than a palm
Dizziness or weakness after a dose

faq.a: Relief is usually noticeable by the end of the first year. The full course takes several years.

faq.q: Can a child have this treatment?
faq.a: Often yes, usually from about age 5. The allergist makes the decision.

reminders.text: Allergy treatment dose tomorrow. If you have a fever or a flare-up, call the clinic before the visit.
